expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output requires the agent to identify an AWS FIS (Fault Injection Simulator) experiment running a PauseVolumeIO action as the root cause of the disk stall — i.e., a self-inflicted change in the account, not an AWS-side fault. It also expects the agent to cite specific evidence (VolumeStalledIOCheck=1, io-performance stalled, attached EBS status check failed, queue above 0 with no completed ops), state when the pause ends, and advise waiting for the experiment to end or stopping it — explicitly avoiding recommending a support case, detach, or stop/start.

The agent's actual response reaches the opposite conclusion: it explicitly states this is 'an AWS-side EBS host-path stall... a backend hardware/host degradation, not a workload or config problem on your end' and checked CloudTrail for volume modifications/attach-detach but did not mention or investigate FIS experiments at all. Its recommended remediation is to wait, then stop/start the instance, then snapshot/swap the volume — which directly contradicts the expected advice (no stop/start) and misses the FIS experiment identification, the PauseVolumeIO action, and the pause end time entirely.

While some surface evidence overlaps (io-performance stalled, attached EBS status check impaired), the agent misses the crucial diagnostic element (queue above 0 with no completed ops indicating an active block) and the FIS experiment as root cause, instead attributing it to an AWS hardware fault. This is a materially wrong conclusion and wrong remediation path (recommending stop/start which the expected output says not to do).
